claims.text: Zirconium-alloy fuel cladding is conventionally coated with elemental Cr.
The intervention places a thin AlNbTiZr multi-element-alloy layer between the zirconium-alloy substrate and the elemental Cr coating.
An AlNbTiZr barrier layer will inhibit elevated-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
Inhibiting Cr–Zr interdiffusion will prevent premature Cr-coating failure.
The modified coating system will maintain oxidation protection during normal subcritical-water operation.
The modified coating system will maintain oxidation protection during accident-relevant high-temperature steam exposure.
The AlNbTiZr layer serves as a structural diffusion barrier between Cr and the Zr-alloy substrate.
The barrier reduces or eliminates diffusion channels that permit Cr and Zr interdiffusion at elevated temperatures.
Suppressing Cr–Zr interdiffusion impedes formation of deleterious intermetallic phases.
Cr–Zr intermetallic phases would otherwise contribute to premature coating failure during high-temperature steam exposure.
Relative to directly Cr-coated zirconium alloy, the barrier-modified system will exhibit significantly less Cr–Zr interdiffusion in high-temperature steam.
Relative to the baseline, the barrier-modified system will have improved Cr-coating integrity and longevity during accident scenarios.
Adding the barrier will not compromise performance during subcritical-water operation.
Normal subcritical-water operation is represented by temperatures below approximately 350°C.
Accident-relevant high-temperature steam exposure is represented by temperatures around or above 800°C.
